actionable_steps.citation: Message of the Avathaars and the Epics — SSS Vol 29 (1996), 1996-05-15
actionable_steps.step: Let your speech be sweet, pleasing and wholesome today; resolve to harm no one by word.

actionable_steps.citation: Spiritual basis of human values — SSS Vol 29 (1996), 1996-01-18
actionable_steps.step: Before you speak or act, pause and consult your conscience: will this cause pain? Wait for its answer before you proceed.

actionable_steps.citation: Spiritual basis of human values — SSS Vol 29 (1996), 1996-01-18
actionable_steps.step: Guard the five gates — no bad looks, bad hearing, bad speech, bad thoughts, bad actions — since harming yourself is also violence.

actionable_steps.citation: Message of the Vedas — SSS Vol 19 (1986)
actionable_steps.step: Cultivate the conviction that the One Supreme dwells in all beings; with that feeling, the urge to harm fades.

definition.citation: The flowers that God loves — SSS Vol 15 (1981 - 82), 1981-05-12
definition.quote: The true meaning of the word is not to cause hurt and harm to any other living being either through your thought, word or deed.

discourses.citation: Message of the Avathaars and the Epics — SSS Vol 29 (1996), 1996-05-15
discourses.quote: Non-violence is not merely refraining from inflicting injuries on others with one's limbs or weapons. Non-violence has to be practised with Thrikarana Shuddhi (purity of mind, tongue and body). There should be no ill-feelings which is a form of violence.

discourses.citation: Message of the Vedas — SSS Vol 19 (1986)
discourses.quote: What we should try to do is to avoid causing any harm to any living being consciously and deliberately. This is Ahimsa. To observe this nonviolence you have to cultivate the feeling that the One Supreme dwells in all beings.

discourses.citation: Idols Are Pointers To Divinity — SSS Vol 35 (2002), 2002-03-12
discourses.quote: Non-violence is the life of the heart... Do not harm anyone. The harm that you inflict on others will boomerang on you.

make_it_real: Hurt no one today — not even with a harsh word or an unkind look. That restraint is your prayer.
title: Non-violence (Ahimsa)

vahinis.quote: How can a person get the attitude of dedicating all activities to the Lord without at the same time being pure in thought, word, and deed? Love, equanimity, rectitude, nonviolence —these are the attendant virtues of the servant of the Lord. How can cruelty and callousness coexist with these virtues?
